holidays.name: Enkutatash
holidays.longDesc: Enkutatash, the Ethiopian New Year, falls on Meskerem 1 (September 11). It marks the end of the rainy season and the beginning of spring. Celebrated with singing, dancing, exchanging of Adey Abeba flowers, and special meals.

holidays.name: Meskel
holidays.longDesc: Meskel celebrates the discovery of the True Cross. The celebration features the Demera bonfire decorated with Meskel daisies, singing, and dancing.

holidays.name: Kidus Mikael
holidays.longDesc: Kidus Mikael (St. Michael) is honored on the 12th of every Ethiopian month. Special church services are held.

holidays.name: Kidus Giorgis
holidays.longDesc: Kidus Giorgis (St. George) is celebrated on the 23rd of every Ethiopian month. St. George is the patron saint of Ethiopia.

holidays.name: Gena
holidays.longDesc: Gena is the Ethiopian Orthodox celebration of Christmas on Tahsas 29 (January 7). Marked by church services and traditional games.

holidays.name: Timkat
holidays.longDesc: Timkat celebrates the baptism of Jesus Christ. Features processions with the Tabot and blessings at bodies of water.

holidays.name: Kidus Yohannes
holidays.longDesc: Commemorates St. John the Baptist on Sene 26. Special church services and prayers.

holidays.name: Adwa Victory Day
holidays.longDesc: Commemorates the Ethiopian victory over Italy at the Battle of Adwa on March 1, 1896. A symbol of African sovereignty.

holidays.name: Workers' Day
holidays.longDesc: International Workers' Day on Miazia 23 (May 1). Honors labor movement and workers' rights.

holidays.name: Patriots' Victory Day
holidays.longDesc: Commemorates the liberation of Ethiopia from Italian occupation on Miazia 27 (May 5), 1941.

holidays.name: Derg Downfall Day
holidays.longDesc: Marks the fall of the Derg military junta on Ginbot 20 (May 28), 1991.

holidays.name: Nations, Nationalities & Peoples' Day
holidays.longDesc: Celebrated on Hidar 29 (December 9). Honors the nations, nationalities, and peoples of Ethiopia.
